articles.summary: Sector rotation is an active investing strategy that shifts equity exposure across the 11 GICS sectors based on US business cycle phases. While intuitively appealing, research shows it carries significant timing and cost risks and may not reliably outperform simpler approaches.
articles.title: Understanding Sector Rotation: A Guide to Business Cycle Investing

articles.summary: Quantitative tightening (QT) is the Federal Reserve's process of shrinking its balance sheet to reduce money supply and normalize interest rates. This guide explains how QT works, its history since 2017, and what it means for investors tracking macro conditions.
articles.title: Quantitative Tightening Explained: How the Fed Shrinks Its Balance Sheet

articles.summary: A bull market is a sustained period of rising stock prices, typically defined by a 20% gain from a recent low. Learn what causes bull markets, how they compare to bear markets, and which investing strategies may help you make the most of rising markets.
articles.title: What Is a Bull Market? Definition, Causes, and Investing Strategies

articles.summary: Historical data shows the S&P 500 has averaged a 4.4% gain during government shutdowns since 1976, with GDP losses typically modest and temporary. The 2025 six-week shutdown — the longest on record — offers a detailed case study of market and economic effects.
articles.title: Government Shutdown Market Impact: What Investors Need to Know

articles.summary: The SEC has approved Nasdaq's proposal to expand trading to a 23-hour, five-days-a-week schedule, targeting a December 2026 launch. Learn how the new Day and Night Sessions work, key trading rules, and how platforms like Webull already offer overnight trading access.
articles.title: Nasdaq 23-Hour Trading: What Investors Need to Know

articles.summary: Election years bring market volatility, but history shows fundamentals like corporate earnings and Fed policy matter more than political outcomes. The S&P 500 has gained in roughly 95% of 12-month periods following midterm elections since 1938.
articles.title: How Election Year Market Impact Shapes U.S. Stock Returns

articles.summary: Market liquidity measures how quickly assets can be bought or sold without significantly moving prices. Learn how bid-ask spreads, trading volume, and order book depth work — and how Webull's real-time tools help US investors assess and manage liquidity risk.
articles.title: Market Liquidity Explained: How US Investors Can Measure and Manage It
